description: Selected public posts by Jevan Goldsmith. Original wording is preserved; longer selections are marked as excerpts.

notes.text: If AI takes the ideas from Crime and Punishment literally I think we are cooked.

notes.title: Names and outcomes
notes.text:
Chat vs Work describes a surface, but not the outcome.

Looking at model names like Luna / Terra / Sol is like expecting me to drive cars I've never seen without telling me if they are supercar, 4wd, hatchback, sedan etc.

Users need to know: fastest, best daily driver, best work horse, cheapest, best at coding, best at research, etc.

Most advice is useless

What people actually need is encouragement and permission to feel into their own spirit.

Surrounded by good examples of people who walk that talk
The courage to follow the thread of our desires, through fear and over all expectation of others is the journey that must make us feel most alive and filled with the least regret.

Ai slop is going to get worse rapidly

Making Trust even more scarce and valuable

So think twice about using it to supplement what you actually want to say

Otherwise people are going to start thinking you aren't saying anything at all

notes.title: Why the mind resists action
notes.text:
Understanding is not a prerequisite for improvement.
We think it is — but it isn’t.

Evolution doesn’t understand anything.
It doesn’t sit around trying to predict what will work.
It just tries things. What breaks disappears. What survives looks intelligent in hindsight.
Consistent small risks taken in private build the conviction to take larger risks in public
Change is the rule not the exception

A question that has occupied my mind a lot recently:

What could Ai not do better than we can?

Hard question.

What is the best in people?

An Ad man of 20th century may have left us a clue:

I plead for charm, flair, showmanship, taste and distinction - David Oglivy
